    Search and facets

    search-and-facets.Rmd

    picsure::searchDictionary() returns matching dictionary entries as a data frame. picsure::facets() narrows a search to a subset — by study, by consent group, etc.

    Plain search 

    library(picsure)
bdc <- picsure::connect(platform = picsure::Platform$BDC_AUTHORIZED, token = Sys.getenv("PICSURE_TOKEN"))

results <- picsure::searchDictionary(bdc, "sex")
head(results)

    Build a FacetSet 

    fs <- picsure::facets(bdc)
fs <- picsure::addFacet(fs, "study_ids", "phs000007")

    addFacet() accepts a vector of values to add several at once:

    fs <- picsure::addFacet(fs, "study_ids", c("phs000200", "phs000286"))

    Remove with removeFacet(fs, key, value). Both functions mutate the underlying Python FacetSet and return it invisibly for chaining.

    Search with facets 

    picsure::searchDictionary(bdc, "sex", facets = fs)

    The server restricts the search to variables inside the facets.

    Lighter payloads

    Pass include_values = FALSE to omit variable values from the response — useful when you only need variable names and descriptions:

    picsure::searchDictionary(bdc, "age", include_values = FALSE)

    The search term is always matched server-side; you receive every matching row. There is no limit or offset — narrow with a more specific term or a facet filter if a search returns too many results.
